data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 proposes that reliability 'reduces to' a choice between omission and misinterpretation, but its own refutation condition and its stated integrative relation both import exactly the factor that reduction would eliminate. If reliability is genuinely reduced to an omission/misinterpretation choice, then a task whose failures are systemic (i.e. systemic misinterpretation) should be cleanly handled by the expert-intuition branch; there should be no residual role for high interdependency or systemic-versus-ommissive structure. Yet the refuting condition is the existence of a high-interdependency task that a checklist-led panel solves more reliably than an expert when the failure mode is systemic. The mere coherence of that refuting case shows that the target content is really claiming 'reliability reduces to error-type distribution, except when task structure overrides it,' which is not a reduction to a two-mode choice. The content thus offers a substantive integration in the same breath as a reduction and lets the two relations compete without resolving which one is being claimed.
